gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each under-$100 camera costs once the hardwire kit its maker requires for parking mode is added: on 2026-11-21 the Vantrue S1 Pro 1CH goes from $79.99 to $104.98-$109.98 and the VIOFO A119 Mini 2 from $159.99 to $177.98, while DDPAI sells camera-plus-kit variants at $49-$99.
standout_why: I opened carcody.com and rottenwifi.com (both cited), plus dealdey.com and dashcamempire.com (top results). All four say parking mode needs a separately sold hardwire kit, and none gives a kit price or a camera-plus-kit total. None says the A119 Mini 2's HDR runs at 30 fps rather than at its headline 60 fps. Carcody and rottenwifi leave the 70mai A400's battery-or-supercapacitor question open, and neither names its sensor. Carcody already has the A119 Mini 2's $99.99 promo against $159.99 regular price, so that part is not new. The cited dashanddrive.com page would not open (certificate error), so it is not compared.
decides: For a shopper who wants parking recording, the Vantrue S1 Pro 1CH no longer fits under $100 once a Vantrue kit is added, and the DDPAI camera-plus-kit variants ($49-$99 store price) are the partner rows that stay inside the budget. For a shopper who does not need parking mode, the S1 Pro 1CH at $79.99 stands as the front-only pick, as in ChatGPT's second chat. The VIOFO A119 Mini 2 is $159.99 on viofo.com today, so it is over the line on its maker's store. The 70mai A400 has a 500 mAh battery, which goes against ChatGPT's own advice to prefer a supercapacitor. DDPAI's resolution, sensor and parking specs were not read (store returned HTTP 429), so a DDPAI row needs its product page opened before it goes in the table.
